clue.text: It is observed in Ecclesiastes that their job is an unending one

definitions.text: It is observed in Ecclesiastes that their job is an unending one

parts.words: It is observed in Ecclesiastes that their job is an unending one
parts.note: Ecclesiastes says 'of making many books there is no end', so people who make books never finish; the cryptic twist is that racecourse betting men are also makers of books

explanation.surface: A scriptural observation about some trade whose work never finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ecclesiastes verse reads 'of making many books there is no end'; taken literally, book-makers have an endless job.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker literally makes books, the very activity the preacher calls endless.

definitions.meaning: to puff is to send out a breath of air
a cuff is a hit with the hand, a punch

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both exhaling air and striking somebody, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Unruly sort of way, to eat asparagus

definitions.text: sort of way, to eat asparagus
definitions.meaning: asparagus is traditionally eaten with the fingers, straight from the hand

explanation.surface: Table manners: a wild style of tackling asparagus.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means uncontrolled, and literally describes food taken in the fingers rather than with cutlery.

parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream, Snout the tinker plays Wall in the mechanicals' play, and the adjective for walls comes from Latin murus

explanation.surface: A question about the part played by one of Shakespeare's mechanicals.
explanation.walkthrough: Snout acts the Wall in Pyramus and Thisbe in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to a wall, which is exactly the role Snout plays.

parts.note: the jack in a pack of cards is also called the knave, and a knave is a rogue, so his misbehaviour is roguish conduct

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a lad called Jack has been naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is the playing card also named the knave.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest roguish conduct is literally the behaviour of a knave, the card also called jack.

indicators.note: sailors handle and rearrange things, so the letters of the first two words are reordered for them

explanation.surface: Something sailors aim at.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of A TARGET rearranged give a boat-racing event, which is indeed something sailors aim to win.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat race meeting is an event that yachtsmen and rowers compete in, so a goal for them.

indicators.note: only a portion of the answer to 12 across is taken, the letters inside it

parts.note: the answer to 12 across, meaning wealthy

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to a section of another entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney passage is a hollow channel through which smoke rises.

clue.text: Girl's name for an old hermitage

definitions.meaning: a woman's first name, as in Petrarch's beloved
historically a group of hermits' cells in the Eastern Church

explanation.surface: A girl's name that once meant a hermits' retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides being a first name, the word denotes a monastic settlement of separate cells for hermits.

clue.text: The cloud-capp'd towers, the gorgeous palaces "—all, in a word, are this

definitions.text: The cloud-capp'd towers, the gorgeous palaces "—all, in a word, are this

parts.words: The cloud-capp'd towers, the gorgeous palaces "—all, in a word, are this
parts.note: Prospero in The Tempest says these towers and palaces shall dissolve and leave not a rack behind, so they are fleeting

explanation.surface: Prospero's speech summed up in a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that vanish like a dissolving pageant are fleeting, quickly fading away.

parts.note: the clue to 10 across says this would turn the river animal into hotter: that change is sounding an H, which phoneticians call breathing on a word

explanation.walkthrough: The clue lives in 10 across: adding a breathed H to OTTER gives HOTTER, and sounding an H is to aspirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetics uses this verb for pronouncing a word with an audible breath, the sound of the letter H.

indicators.note: 9 down is the sounding of an initial breath, which the answer lacks; take that breathed letter away from the last word and the answer remains

explanation.surface: Something that would make a fire blaze more fiercely.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 down is ASPIRATE: breathing an H before the answer gives HOTTER, so HOTTER less its H is the answer. A burn is a Scottish stream, where this animal lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The water mammal of Scottish streams becomes the word for warmer once a breathy letter is sounded before it.

clue.text: Not a sugar mixture; in fact, anything but sweet

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so these letters are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: A sugarless blend that is far from sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: These are aromatic bitters used in cocktails, so the opposite of sweet.

definitions.meaning: a tributary, a smaller stream flowing into a larger river

explanation.surface: A rich brook.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means rich, and as a noun it names a tributary flowing into a river.

parts.note: the closing letters of the answer to 9 down, which also form a word meaning angry

explanation.walkthrough: 9 down is ASPIRATE, which ends with the letters of a word meaning furious.
explanation.definitionFit: The last five letters of the breathing word form an everyday adjective for angry.

clue.text: From which solid hopes may be forthcoming

definitions.text: From which solid hopes may be forthcoming

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase come forth in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Something promising that could yield firm expectations.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffling SOLID HOPES gives the answer; goods damaged by display in a store are where hopes for a bargain come from.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods slightly damaged from being displayed in a store are sold cheaply, raising hopes of a bargain.

parts.note: what people say is passed on by word of mouth, so a report heard from others

explanation.surface: A gossip passing on unconfirmed news.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumour is unverified report picked up from what other people say.

parts.note: a corkscrew turns round and round in a helix as it enters the cork

explanation.surface: A question about how a wine opener operates.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes motion in a winding helix, which is the corkscrew's path.

indicators.note: a building that collapses falls into a heap, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A picture house falls down.
explanation.walkthrough: The collapsed letters of A CINEMA describe the feeble state of a failing picture house.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale and lacking vigour, which is how a failing, collapsing business looks.

parts.note: can be read as an adjective, done on purpose, or as a verb, think things over

explanation.definitionFit: Something planned in advance is premeditated, and to ponder is to have thought carefully, both senses fitting.

parts.note: the anonymous song The Vicar of Bray has the line about George arriving in this sort of time, meaning a time of plenty

explanation.surface: A line from an old song with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vicar of Bray says George I came over in 'pudding time', a phrase for good times or the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word completes the stock phrase meaning a time of plenty, as the song has it.

clue.text: Add earth to a cosmetic, and the result is simply hellish

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun meaning hell: 'simply' signals the result is hell itself

parts.note: Ge is the Greek earth goddess, and the word appears in geography
henna is a reddish dye for hair and skin

explanation.surface: A recipe: mixing soil into make-up gives something awful.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical valley of burning is used as a name for hell, so the result is simply hell.

clue.text: It is in the nature of a quid pro quo

definitions.text: It is in the nature of a quid pro quo

parts.words: It is in the nature of a quid pro quo
parts.note: something given in return for a service, an archaic word for a recompense

explanation.surface: Describing something given in exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic literary word for reward, which is a return for what one has done.

parts.note: to win is to gain
aye, also spelt ay, means yes

explanation.surface: Someone disagrees, yet the vote goes in favour.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny or speak against is a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: One or more than one item in a composer's output

definitions.text: One or more than one item in a composer's output

parts.words: One or more than one item in a composer's output
parts.note: the word is a single staged musical drama, and also the Latin plural of opus, several numbered works

explanation.surface: Counting the works a composer has produced.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both one sung stage work and the plural of opus, a composer's numbered pieces.

clue.text: " She took me to her grot, And there she wept and sigh'd full sore " (Keats)

definitions.text: " She took me to her grot, And there she wept and sigh'd full sore " (Keats)

parts.words: " She took me to her grot, And there she wept and sigh'd full sore " (Keats)
parts.note: in La Belle Dame sans Merci the line reads 'She took me to her ... grot', the missing adjective meaning fairy-like

explanation.surface: A quotation from Keats with a word left out.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing adjective describes the fairy lady's cave as belonging to the fairy folk.

indicators.note: the old explicit instruction to rearrange the letters given before it

explanation.surface: An alluring piece of headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine mesh caps worn over the hair are a kind of hat, and could be fetching.

clue.text: A piece to Julia from Herrick

definitions.text: A piece to Julia from Herrick

parts.words: A piece to Julia from Herrick
parts.note: Robert Herrick wrote The ...-Piece, to Julia, so the missing first part of the title is wanted

explanation.surface: A poem sent by Herrick to his Julia.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's title joins this word to piece, naming the evening hours when it is set.

parts.note: the initials of the Distinguished Service Order, a British military award written after a holder's name

explanation.walkthrough: The Distinguished Service Order is a British medal for officers; its holders put its initials after their names.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-nominal initials showing an honour for gallantry are literally letters that mark distinction.

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
cats are felines

explanation.surface: A large number of cats.
explanation.walkthrough: Cats proverbially have nine lives, so many cats imply many lives saved.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropes thrown to save people, punning on cats and their nine lives.

indicators.note: the word for a head is cut off the town's name

parts.note: Gateshead is a town in north-east England, across the Tyne from Newcastle

explanation.surface: A northern city lacking its head.
explanation.walkthrough: GATESHEAD is a town on the Tyne in north-east England; taking off its HEAD leaves the answer, and old cities had walls with these entrances.
explanation.definitionFit: Barred entrances in a wall or fence, what remains of the northern town's name.

parts.note: Christopher Smart's Song to David ends 'Determined, dared, and ...', the missing word meaning accomplished

explanation.surface: A line of Smart's poem with its final word gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing word of the line means accomplished, finished, completing the alliterative trio.

parts.note: female figures carved as columns literally hold up a building's roof, not bandits staging a robbery

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold-up' suggests a robbery; here it means supporting a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculpted women used as pillars, like those on the Erechtheion in Athens, bear the weight above.
